title: Wagon cup holder: v3.1, clears the strut and latch
subtitle: Clip stays on the side rail · cup module lifts off its dovetail · moved out to clear the end latch and strut · shown assembled, in print orientation · millimetres
scale_note: Real size, shown assembled. The rail is your 22.3 mm tube. The tumbler is from retailer listings (70 mm base, 89 mm widest). The two wireframe blocks are the red latch and diagonal strut at each end of your 120 mm clear stretch. They are APPROXIMATE: only the ~26 mm reach is from you, and I assumed they sit only beyond the clear stretch. It is drawn in print orientation: the rail axis is vertical here and the cup lies on its side. In use the rail is horizontal and the cup stands upright, hanging off the outside of it.
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v3.1: you said the strut and red latch reach about 26 mm out past the bar, the same at both ends, and the 120 mm is the clear stretch between them. I moved the cup out so the module's web starts 40 mm from the bar axis, about 3 mm clear of the worst-case reading of the strut and latch (26 mm past the bar's outer surface). The module is 88 mm long inside the 120 mm window, so 16 mm to spare each end, and the clip is centred on it. The cost is more twist on the clip, about 0.82 N·m for a full cup (was 0.67), still within what the bolt clamp should hold. Please check on the real wagon: (1) does the diagonal strut slope in under the cup? The cup base is 60 mm below the bar axis. If it does, I will raise the cup. (2) is anything else outboard of the bar inside the clear stretch? (3) does the empty clip block folding? Clamp the 15 mm test slice on the bar and fold. Then print the three small test pieces.
